cap: Hashimoto thyroiditis read as a chain of cause and effect: autoimmune attack marked by anti-TPO and antithyroglobulin antibodies, a biopsy with germinal centers and Hürthle cells, loss of follicles that lowers free T4 and raises TSH, and the long-term risk of primary thyroid B-cell lymphoma.
teach: Each panel is caused by the one before it. The autoimmune attack destroys follicles; the biopsy shows the lymphoid reaction and the damaged follicular cells; fewer follicles means less T4, so the pituitary releases more TSH, which is why the lab pattern is primary hypothyroidism. Chronic lymphoid stimulation explains the lymphoma risk.
